body:
## Why

`docs/specs/operating-stack.md` §5 routes `build.ladder-start` to the assignment tier's channel and states **"Escalation per F8 is a fresh attempt"**. Nothing implements that escalation.

`planSeats` resolves each ticket's seat ONCE PER RUN, and `advanceTicket`'s two-strike loop re-dispatches with the same deps — so a ticket that a cheap model cannot complete burns BOTH strikes on that cheap model and fails. The ladder never climbs.

This is the economic premise of the whole barbell: slack work starts cheap precisely BECAUSE a failure escalates to something stronger. Without it, starting cheap is just a cheaper way to fail. `assign.mjs`'s `resolveBudget` already provisions for the escalation (`ladder` mode returns starting tier + one frontier regeneration), so the budget is allocated for an attempt that never happens.

Not a regression — fleet has never escalated. The gap is newly VISIBLE because T151 made "which model ran this attempt" an explicit, recorded property.

## What to build

1. **The ladder contract (`packages/quartermaster`)** — a pure function over the §5 rules: given a seat's starting channel, its derived job, its assignment mode, and a 1-based attempt number, return the channel that attempt must run on. Attempt 1 is always the starting channel; each later attempt climbs one rung along `cheap → mid → frontier` and STOPS at the top rather than indexing past it. Only a `build.ladder-start` job in `mode: "ladder"` climbs.
2. **Pre-resolved rungs (`planSeats`)** — the escalation seats are resolved from the registry at planning time, alongside the starting seat, so dispatch never needs the registry and the dry-run can show the whole ladder. A registry that validates has every §4a channel present, so every rung resolves or the run has already failed closed at load.
3. **Per-attempt dispatch (`live-deps`)** — dispatch selects the adapter AND model for the attempt's rung, not the run's starting seat. `provision` runs for every DISTINCT adapter in the ticket's ladder, so an escalated strike never lands on an unprovisioned harness (only `claude-code` provisions today, and it writes the worktree allowlist its worker needs).
4. **Visibility (§11 q4)** — the §8a dispatch usage carrier records the channel that ACTUALLY ran plus the channel it escalated from. No separate `kind: "escalation"` telemetry event is emitted: the carrier is already written once per dispatch and already carries `channel`, `transport` and `registryDigest`, no §8c monitor consumes a ladder-escalation event, and a second producer for the same fact would invite double-counting. The transcript header names the channel too, so the human-facing log and the ledger agree.

### Binding rules

- **`mode`, not just `job`, decides.** A ticket below the rail-density floor is assigned `tier: frontier, mode: direct` while still DERIVING `build.ladder-start` when its float is non-zero. Keying escalation on the job alone would escalate a ticket the router deliberately routed direct. Escalation requires BOTH `job === "build.ladder-start"` and `mode === "ladder"`.
- **F8: escalation is a fresh attempt, never a rescue.** The existing strike-2 fix charter and worktree state are unchanged; only the supply changes.
- **A recorded channel must be one that ran.** An entry naming the starting channel for a dispatch that escalated is the same "label proves nothing about what ran" failure §4c closed for `model`.
- **`packages/model-router/lib/assign.mjs` is consumed as emitted** and must not change. Asserted as an acceptance criterion rather than declared as a `rails` entry on purpose: a rail would freeze it for every PR in the repo until this ticket completes, which is exactly the block this ticket had to pay off in T151 before it could start.

## Acceptance criteria

- A ladder-start ticket in `mode: "ladder"` whose seat starts on `cheap` dispatches strike 1 on the cheap seat's adapter and model, and strike 2 on the `mid` seat's adapter and model — asserted on the argv the adapter ACTUALLY rendered (the recorded spawn call), never on a plan object or a seat lookup. Verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/ladder-escalation.test.mjs`.
- A `mode: "direct"` ticket re-dispatches strike 2 on the SAME channel, adapter and model as strike 1, asserted on the rendered argv — INCLUDING the below-floor case that derives job `build.ladder-start` with `mode: "direct"`, which must not climb. Verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/ladder-escalation.test.mjs`.
- Escalation stops at the top: for every starting channel, attempts 1 through 6 never index past `frontier`, and a ladder starting on `frontier` returns `frontier` for every attempt. Verified by `node --test packages/quartermaster/test/escalate.test.mjs`.
- The §8a dispatch usage carrier for an escalated strike records `channel` equal to the channel that RAN and `escalatedFrom` equal to the starting channel; a non-escalated dispatch records the starting channel and NO `escalatedFrom` key. Verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/ladder-escalation.test.mjs`.
- A ladder whose rungs name DIFFERENT adapters provisions each distinct adapter before the pipeline starts — asserted by observing the provision calls, so an escalated strike cannot run on an unprovisioned harness. Verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/ladder-escalation.test.mjs`.
- `fleet run --dry-run` prints, for each ladder-start seat, the starting channel AND the rungs escalation may climb to, so the plan never implies a single fixed model; a direct-mode seat prints no ladder. Driven through the real CLI in a throwaway repo with a real operator registry. Verified by `node --test packages/quartermaster/test/escalation-dryrun.test.mjs`.
- `docs/specs/operating-stack.md` §5's `build.ladder-start` row names the implementing module instead of only asserting F8, and §11 open question 4 is resolved in the spec text with the decision recorded in item 4 above. Verified by inspecting `git diff origin/main -- docs/specs/operating-stack.md`.
- The router's output is untouched and every affected segment is green: `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- packages/model-router/lib/assign.mjs` exits 0, and `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` exits 0.

## Context

- Issue #401. Surfaced by an adversarial-review round on the T151 branch; T151 shipped the per-run seat resolution this ticket makes per-attempt.
- Code: `packages/fleet/lib/scheduler.mjs` (already passes `strike` to the dispatch effect), `packages/fleet/lib/live-deps.mjs` (`seatFor`, `adapterFor`, `recordDispatchUsage`), `packages/fleet/lib/quartermaster.mjs` (`planSeats`), `packages/quartermaster/lib/channels.mjs` (`LADDER_TIER_CHANNELS`), `packages/model-router/lib/assign.mjs` (`resolveBudget`, read-only).
- Sibling gap, deliberately NOT in scope: #396 — `transport` is recorded but not load-bearing at dispatch, so two rungs differing only by transport still execute identically.
title: Ladder escalation: re-derive the dispatch seat per attempt so a failed strike climbs the channel ladder (#401)
